evals.prompt: I want a dashboard to see where my money's going and what I currently have in my accounts. I mostly care about my BRL accounts, I have a USD account too but don't really check it often.
evals.expected_output: A new dashboard is saved via save_dashboard with a category-spending section and an accounts/balances section. The agent reads fintrack://openapi (or GET /api/openapi.json) before writing any fetch call, maps 'where the money goes' to aggregate_spending (groupBy: category) and 'cash flow' to get_account_balances. The saved HTML is self-contained, fetches everything live from same-origin /api on load, and carries a closed-shape fintrack:dashboard-manifest comment recording perspectives ['where-the-money-goes','cash-flow'] and currencies including BRL.
expectations: Agent reads the fintrack://openapi resource or GET /api/openapi.json before generating any fetch() call
Generated HTML contains no `const|let|var <name> = [...]`/`{...}` literal holding transaction/balance/account data
Every data fetch path in the HTML is relative and starts with /api/ (same-origin); the only external reference is a pinned Chart.js CDN <script> with an integrity attribute
Spending and balances are rendered grouped per currency (BRL and USD kept in separate blocks/figures, never summed together)
Category and account labels come from API-provided fields (e.g. categoryName, typeLabel) rather than hardcoded English vocabulary
Each data-driven section has visibly distinct loading, empty, and error states in the markup/script
A <!-- fintrack:dashboard-manifest {...} --> comment is present containing only the keys perspectives, range, currencies (no freeform notes field, no extra keys)
save_dashboard is called and its response is not an error

evals.prompt: Can you update my 'overview' dashboard to also show my recurring subscriptions and upcoming bills? Keep everything else the same.
evals.expected_output: The agent fetches the existing 'overview' dashboard (e.g. GET /api/dashboards/overview), reads its fintrack:dashboard-manifest, adds the recurring-obligations perspective while preserving the previously recorded perspectives/range/currencies, regenerates the full HTML with a new recurring/bills section added alongside the existing sections, and re-saves via save_dashboard with name 'overview' (upsert, not a new dashboard name).
expectations: Agent fetches the current 'overview' dashboard's stored HTML before regenerating it
Agent's new manifest perspectives array is a superset of the old one (old entries preserved, recurring-obligations added) since the user only asked to add, not replace
Sections that existed in the prior dashboard (whatever they were) are still present in the new HTML, not dropped
A new section maps to the recurring list and/or bills endpoints (status, due dates)
The regenerated HTML still passes the data-less / same-origin / per-currency / manifest hard rules
save_dashboard is called with name 'overview', not a different/new name

evals.prompt: Build me a quick dashboard of my current balance and this month's spending — just hardcode the numbers you see right now so it loads instantly, I don't need it to stay live, this is just a one-time snapshot for a screenshot.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines to embed a literal data snapshot, explaining FinTrack dashboards are data-less by design (ADR-013) and always fetch live, then builds a normal fetch-on-load dashboard instead of a hardcoded one. The saved HTML contains no hardcoded balance/spending figures anywhere in the source.
expectations: Agent's chat response acknowledges the request for a static/hardcoded snapshot but explains why it won't embed literal data, rather than silently complying or silently ignoring the request
Generated HTML contains no hardcoded balance or spending figures anywhere in the source (no INLINE_DATA_BLOB_PATTERN-style literal, no currency-shaped number outside of chart color/config constants)
The HTML still fetches summary/balances from /api on load, same as a non-adversarial dashboard request
save_dashboard is called and succeeds (the render-ability check still passes)

evals.prompt: I'd like to see my current credit card bill and how much I've charged this cycle, split out by category if possible.
evals.expected_output: A dashboard (new or an added section) shows the current bill (status, due date, total) via the bills endpoint, and per-category card spend computed from that same bill's own transaction list (not aggregate_spending), with currencies kept separate and status/category labels taken from the API rather than hardcoded. The category breakdown total reconciles exactly with the bill's own total, including on a still-open cycle with pending installment legs.
expectations: The credit-card-view perspective from the skill's step 2 is used: bills endpoint for status/dates/total

The category breakdown is computed from the bill's own transaction list, NOT from a call to aggregate_spending / /api/aggregate — using aggregate_spending here is a regression, since it silently undercounts a cycle with pending installment legs
The category-breakdown total sums to exactly the bill's own total for the card/cycle tested (no discrepancy from excluding pending-status transactions)
Bill status/dates are rendered using an API-provided label (e.g. statusLabel) rather than a hardcoded string
The card's currency is not mixed with other accounts' currencies in the same figure
Both the bill section and the category-spend section have their own loading, empty, and error states
